title: Hunts FH-042S: Player answer form and authoring for choices and Mystery

source.ref: Split from FH-042 (2026-11-16): the branch engine, the server-only answer check and the claim path shipped dark; the screens and authoring move here.

detail:
Requires FH-042, FH-030S. The engine and the claim door accept choices and Mystery answers, but no screen reaches them. Build: (1) the player answer form on the play and scan screens, passing the answer to claimAsPlayer and wording answer_required, answer_wrong (attempts left, the hint), answer_locked (point at the fallback stop) and a closed branch, per docs/NAMING.md and docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md; (2) the projection for a locked-out Mystery, so projectForPlayer stops naming it as the next stop once its attempts are used; (3) authoring through a lib/studio entity: choice_group, fallback_group, mission kind answer, and the answer itself written only through hashAnswer (lib/hunts/mystery.ts) so the plain answer is never stored, with validateGraph blockers shown before publish; (4) a decision, recorded as an ADR if taken, on whether hunt_claim_apply should itself refuse a second member of a choice group, which would close the staff-approval gap named in FH-042 and needs a migration through the serial database gate; (5) a pgTAP or live two-session run of two branches claimed at once against real Postgres, which the FH-042 tests only model. Done when: a player can answer a Mystery on a phone, a wrong and a locked answer read clearly, a creator can publish a fork and a Mystery without touching JSON, and the two-session race is recorded against the real database. Owner role: Game systems. Hunts switches stay OFF. 2026-11-18: part (1) built, dark. claimStopAction (app/(main)/hunts/[slug]/play/actions.ts) takes the player's answer and words answer_required, answer_wrong (tries left and the hint), answer_locked (head to the stand-in stop) and a closed branch; components/hunts/claim-stop-form.tsx shows the answer field when the open stop is a Mystery or the server asks; the scan POST lands a Mystery verdict on the public Trail page, which sends the player to the play page to answer. Still owed: (2) the locked-out Mystery projection; (3) authoring. Authoring needs a design call first: lib/hunts/draft.test.ts pins the stop repeat's field kinds (longtext, text, text, toggle x3) and that every stop field survives a save, so the Mystery, fork and stand-in controls cannot simply join the stops repeat; they need their own repeat or entity that writes choice_group, fallback_group, kind answer and an answer_hash made by hashAnswer in the save action (the hunt_missions columns already exist, so no SQL). (4) and (5) unchanged. The probe stays red until (3) lands.

2026-11-18: closed by its probe. Part (3) built per ADR-1977: Trail challenges are their own list (hunt_versions.policy.challenges, lib/hunts/challenges.ts, the challenges repeat of HUNT_MANIFEST, components/hunts/trail-challenges.tsx on the editor's shape step), saved by saveChallengesAction (app/(main)/hunts/challenge-actions.ts), which hashes a typed answer with hashAnswer and returns only answerSet. Publish writes kind answer, answer_hash, choice_group and fallback_group, and the checklist words the author's blockers before validateGraph. The stops list and lib/hunts/draft.test.ts are unchanged; a Trail with no challenges publishes as before. Tests: lib/hunts/challenges.test.ts, app/(main)/hunts/challenge-actions.test.ts. Still owed, filed as FH-042T: (2) the locked-out Mystery projection, (4) the decision on hunt_claim_apply refusing a second choice-group member (needs a migration), (5) the live two-session race, and a real-phone pass.
